html:
The Gurjara-Pratiharas were the leading power of north India in the 9th century, ruling from Kannauj after 816. On the 800 and 900 maps they hold the broad middle of the north.

The family rose in Rajasthan and Malwa in the 8th century. Its early king Nagabhata I is remembered for helping to stop the Arabs of Sindh. In the long Tripartite Struggle against the Palas of Bengal and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan, Nagabhata II won Kannauj in 816.

Their peak came under Mihira Bhoja, who ruled from about 836 to 885. An Arab merchant of the time praised the size of his cavalry and called him the greatest enemy of Islam in India. A Rashtrakuta raid sacked Kannauj in the 10th century, and the empire broke into smaller states. The next page, the late Pratiharas, follows the decline until Mahmud of Ghazni took Kannauj in 1018.
sum: The Gurjara-Pratiharas were the leading power of north India in the 9th century, ruling from Kannauj after 816. On the 800 and 900 maps they hold the broad middle of the north.
